## Context

tsk-1hq's own repro (pick -> `fgos edit --verify ...` -> `fgos return`) is
real: `src/state/store.mjs:1101-1105` (`settleClaim`) still throws
`conflict` on any `preClaimRevision` mismatch, `editWork`
(`store.mjs:362-469`) never touches the claim record, and
`preClaimRevision` is written exactly once, at claim time
(`src/runner/claim-port.mjs:317`) -- confirmed fresh against this repo's
current `main` (`d679ae0c`), not just the item's 2026-08-25 read.

The gap is broader than `fgos edit`: `moveStage`
(`store.mjs:1382-1404`, the door every `fgos discover`/`fgos plan` stage
move calls) also never touches the claim record, and
`src/state/replay.mjs:406-428` confirms a stage move mutates the same
`work[id]` object `getItemDurableRevision`
(`src/state/runtime-coordination.mjs:49-53`) hashes -- so any durable
`work[id]` write during `doing`, a stage move included, can trip this,
not only an explicit edit.

**More importantly: this looks like a duplicate of in-flight `tsk-1ht`**
("settleClaim's revision-CAS check has no reconcile path, refuses return
for any claimed item edited...", `status: doing`, `stage: planning`).
`tsk-1ht`'s own branch (`fgw/tsk-1ht`, commit `f6e7c63d` "fix(state):
settleClaim reconciles same-writer revision drift instead of refusing")
already has a real fix committed but NOT merged into `main`
(`git merge-base --is-ancestor f6e7c63d main` fails). That fix adds
`revisionDriftIsSelfCaused` to `settleClaim`: reconciles only when every
event on the item since the claim's `acquiredAt` carries
`payload.writer.id === claim.writerId`, else it still refuses -- and per
its own `plan.md` this already covers both `editWork`- and
`moveStage`-caused drift, not just `fgos edit`.

## Why this matters

Whether tsk-1hq should be marked wontfix/duplicate of tsk-1ht, given an
explicit `deps` on it and parked until `tsk-1ht` merges, or continue
independently is a scope decision this stage should not make silently --
planning would otherwise re-derive and re-implement a fix that already
exists, unreviewed and unmerged, on another branch. A person needs to
decide: merge/prioritize `tsk-1ht` first and close `tsk-1hq` as a
duplicate, or some other resolution (e.g. `tsk-1ht`'s fix turns out
insufficient/wrong on review and `tsk-1hq` should proceed as the real
fix instead).
